verdict: Avoid new gold-jewellery manufacturing exposure in Jaipur for now; lend only to organised, low-leverage, high-turnover manufacturers with tight gold-metal control, and decline the rest.
title: Jaipur gold jewellery manufacturing: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**A Jaipur gold-jewellery unit buys bullion or scrap, converts it into ornaments through karigars, and sells to wholesalers and retailers on thin making charges.** Cash is tied in gold inventory and receivables, not in plant; the metal is the balance sheet. Peer results show the model can scale fast when demand is there — Shanti Gold's Q4 FY26 revenue grew 121.65% YoY [4] and Q3 FY26 revenue rose 110.06% YoY [6] — but that is peer performance, not Jaipur. **So when a proposal lands, check the gold-metal account and inventory days first; if the unit cannot show karigar-wise metal reconciliation, ask for the stock statement and insurer's cover before anything else.**

## Where value and cash sit
**Value sits in making charges and design, but cash sits in working capital, and that is where the risk is.** ICRA notes working-capital intensity of 15–20% and expects it to rise with gold prices [10], and flags intense competition from unorganised players limiting pricing flexibility [8]. Margins are real but thin: NGJL ran 11.0% operating and 5.7% net margin in FY2025 [9]; Ashapuri's EBITA margin was 8.78% [7]. **So price the limit to the cycle, not the festive peak; if the borrower asks for a limit sized to peak inventory, ask for the off-season stock statement and the last two years' drawing power.**

## What has changed now
**Local demand has softened and the official data pack is negative on Rajasthan.** Gold fell ₹10,700 and silver ₹44,000 in the month, with buyers cautious ahead of Diwali [1]; a June 2026 report recorded a slump in Jaipur trade after the PM's appeal to abstain from buying yellow metal [3] — that source is five months old, treat it as context. Rajasthan GST collections are -4.7% Apr-to-date versus India +6.1%, and electricity demand +4.0% versus India +9.5% [D]. Nationally, bank credit is +33.0% YoY against output +3.8% [D], and the repo is 5.5% with a tightening stance [D]. **So do not read a festive order book as recovery; if the borrower's sales are flat while its limit utilisation is rising, ask why the gap is being funded by the bank.**

## Where to grow, and how to grow safely
**Pursue organised manufacturers with 18-carat and 9/14-carat lines for younger buyers — Sky Gold's call notes 18-carat taking share from 22-carat, with 22-carat still 70–75% of sales [5].** Avoid single-promoter units with no metal audit, no hallmarking discipline and heavy bullion-price exposure. Structure as a cash-flow limit against verified stock and receivables, with a margin on gold value and a personal guarantee.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the metal, not the narrative.** A borrower extending credit terms to retailers, or holding inventory through a price fall, is the first sign. ICRA flags regulatory risk and bullion-import restrictions as sector-wide exposures [8], and rising gold prices lifting working-capital intensity [10]. **If receivables days stretch beyond the borrower's own two-year average, or gold-on-lease exceeds owned stock, stop fresh disbursement and ask for the ageing.**
watch: Inventory days rise above the borrower's two-year average -> freeze fresh disbursement, ask for karigar-wise metal account
GST turnover falls two quarters running while limit utilisation rises -> reduce limit, seek additional collateral
Receivables days stretch beyond own two-year average -> stop disbursement, ask for retailer-wise ageing
Monthly gold price and local demand (Jaipur bullion reports)
Sustained price fall with flat offtake -> revalue stock cover and reassess margin
